rows.grounds: compound denoting the moment prior to the act of perceiving an object; locative sense
refers back to the consciousness-goddesses (saṃviddevyaḥ) described in the preceding verse

items.question: Why does consciousness withdraw spontaneously prior to the perception of any knowable object?
premises: Consciousness is characterized as all-pervading and foundational in the preceding context.
The perception of a knowable object marks a directed outward movement.
A state prior to object-perception is identified as a locus of reversal.
items.inference: Therefore, consciousness itself turns back inward before engaging with any knowable object.
uncertainties: The exact referent of sā could be taken as consciousness in general or specifically the saṃviddevyaḥ of verse 74.
items.plain_english: Before the perception of any knowable object arises, she turns back by herself.
